name: Chicago Monthly Crime Counts
citation: City of Chicago. "Crimes - 2001 to Present." Chicago Data Portal, data.cityofchicago.org/Public-Safety/Crimes-2001-to-Present/ijzp-q8t2. Accessed 15 July 2026.
license: U.S./municipal public data (City of Chicago open data; FRED/Federal Reserve; Open-Meteo CC-BY 4.0). Free to use and redistribute.
description:
Monthly count of reported crime incidents in Chicago (all offense types), 2001-present, with the known-future weather + macro drivers of crime. Application: predictive police shift/beat allocation. Covariate glossary:
- reported crime incidents: total reported crime incidents per month, City of Chicago open data (ijzp-q8t2).
- chicago mean temperature: monthly-mean 2m air temperature at Chicago, degrees Celsius (Open-Meteo archive) - heat drives the summer violence peak.
- us unemployment rate: U.S. civilian unemployment rate, percent, seasonally adjusted (FRED UNRATE).
preprocessing: 1. Pulled target from the cited City of Chicago open-data API (Socrata, ijzp-q8t2).
2. Aligned covariates (Open-Meteo temperature monthly-mean; FRED macro) onto the target's time index.
3. Incident-level records counted per month to form the monthly series.
4. Forward/back-filled sparse covariate gaps; dropped provisional/partial tail periods.
5. Single shared ISO-8601 time index; no calendar columns.
